taskVersion.name: deadline-math-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Standard set, reasoning allowed. Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On September 30, 2026, Eastern Time (ET) is in Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4), and Madrid is in Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2), which is 6 hours ahead of ET. 

Adding 6 hours to 5:00 PM (17:00) gives 11:00 PM (23:00) on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru is in the Peru Time (PET) zone, which is UTC-5 year-round (Peru does not observe daylight saving time). 

Subtracting 5 hours from 12:00 UTC on July 15, 2026 gives 07:00 on July 15, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to Tokyo local time (Japan Standard Time, JST):

1. **CEST (Central European Summer Time)** is UTC+2.
2. **JST (Japan Standard Time)** is UTC+9.
3. Tokyo is 7 hours ahead of CEST ($9 - 2 = 7$ hours).

Adding 7 hours to June 1, 2026, at 9:00 AM (09:00) gives June 1, 2026, at 16:00 (4:00 PM).

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Madrid:

1. **PDT (Pacific Daylight Time)** is UTC-7. 
   - October 11, 2026, at 11:59 PM PDT corresponds to October 12, 2026, at 06:59 UTC.
2. **Madrid, Spain** observes Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) in mid-October.
   - October 12, 2026, at 06:59 UTC + 2 hours is October 12, 2026, at 08:59 CEST.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert March 3, 2026, at 11:59 PM PST to Madrid time (CET):

1. **PST (Pacific Standard Time)** is UTC-8.
2. **Madrid (Central European Time)** is UTC+1 in early March (Daylight Saving Time has not yet started in either region).
3. Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PST.
4. Adding 9 hours to March 3, 2026, at 23:59 PST results in March 4, 2026, at 08:59 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert 10:00 AM CET on February 2, 2026, to Los Angeles local time:

1. **Central European Time (CET)** in February is UTC+1.
2. **Pacific Standard Time (PST)** in Los Angeles in February is UTC-8.
3. Los Angeles is 9 hours behind CET.

Subtracting 9 hours from 10:00 AM on February 2, 2026 gives 1:00 AM on February 2, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Lima, Peru:

1. Japan Standard Time (JST) is UTC+9.
2. Lima, Peru is on Peru Time (PET), which is UTC-5 (with no daylight saving time).
3. The difference is 14 hours (JST is 14 hours ahead of PET).
4. Subtracting 14 hours from May 5, 2026, at 08:00 JST gives May 4, 2026, at 18:00 PET.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 28, 2026:
- Pacific Time (PT) is in Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7) as US daylight saving time ends on November 1, 2026.
- Madrid is in Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) as European daylight saving time ended on October 25, 2026.

The difference is 8 hours ahead of PT. Adding 8 hours to October 28, 2026 at 23:59 gives October 29, 2026 at 07:59.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 30, 2026:
- Eastern Time (ET) is still on Daylight Saving Time (EDT, UTC-4), as US daylight saving ends on November 1, 2026.
- Madrid, Spain has already switched back to standard time (CET, UTC+1) on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026).

Therefore, Madrid is 5 hours ahead of ET:
9:00 AM EDT + 5 hours = 14:00 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 27, 2026:
- Central European Time (CET) is UTC+1 (Daylight Saving Time in Europe ends on October 25, 2026). 18:00 CET corresponds to 17:00 UTC.
- New York is on Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4 (US Daylight Saving Time ends on November 1, 2026).
- 17:00 UTC minus 4 hours is 13:00 EDT.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in your local time (Madrid, Spain):

1. **Pacific Time (PT) on November 2, 2026:** Daylight Saving Time in the US ends on Sunday, November 1, 2026, so Pacific Time will be Pacific Standard Time (PST, UTC−8). 11:59 PM PST is 23:59 on November 2, 2026 (07:59 UTC on November 3, 2026).
2. **Madrid Time on November 3, 2026:** Daylight Saving Time in Europe ends on Sunday, October 25, 2026, so Madrid will be on Central European Time (CET, UTC+1).
3. Adding 9 hours to 11:59 PM PST on November 2 gives 08:59 AM on November 3, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On March 20, 2026, the US is observing Daylight Saving Time (PDT, which is UTC-7), while Madrid, Spain is still observing Central European Time (CET, which is UTC+1). 

Madrid is 8 hours ahead of Pacific Time:
- March 20, 2026, at 11:59 PM PDT + 8 hours = March 21, 2026, at 07:59 AM CET.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On March 25, 2026:
- Central European Time (CET) is UTC+1 (Daylight Saving Time in Europe begins March 29, 2026), so 12:00 PM CET is 11:00 UTC.
- Los Angeles is on Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7 (Daylight Saving Time in the US began March 8, 2026).
- 11:00 UTC minus 7 hours is 04:00 (4:00 AM) on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 12, 2026, Eastern Time (ET) is in Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4), and Madrid, Spain is in Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2). 

Madrid is 6 hours ahead of ET. 
12:00 AM EDT (midnight at the start of October 12, 2026) corresponds to 06:00 CEST on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Madrid, Spain:

1. **AoE (Anywhere on Earth)** corresponds to the time zone **UTC-12:00**. 
   - 23:59 AoE on October 9, 2026 is **11:59 UTC on October 10, 2026**.
2. On October 9–10, Madrid observes Central European Summer Time (**CEST**), which is **UTC+2**.
3. Adding 2 hours to the UTC time gives **13:59** on **October 10, 2026**.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert 12:00 PM PT (Pacific Time, which is Pacific Daylight Time UTC-7 in August) to Madrid local time (Central European Summer Time, UTC+2):

Madrid is 9 hours ahead of Pacific Time in August.
12:00 PM + 9 hours = 21:00 on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Madrid:

1. **Indian Standard Time (IST):** UTC+5:30  
   Deadline: November 10, 2026, at 23:59 IST = 18:29 UTC.
2. **Madrid Local Time (CET):** On November 10, 2026, Spain observes Central European Time (UTC+1).  
   18:29 UTC + 1 hour = 19:29 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the deadline to your local time in Lima, Peru:

1. Nepal Time (NPT) is UTC+5:45.
   - April 2, 2026, at 5:00 PM (17:00 NPT) corresponds to 11:15 AM UTC on April 2, 2026.
2. Lima, Peru Time (PET) is UTC-5 (no daylight saving time).
   - 11:15 AM UTC minus 5 hours is 6:15 AM (06:15) on April 2, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the deadline in Madrid time:

1. **Adelaide Time Zone:** On October 6, 2026, Adelaide is observing Australian Central Daylight Time (ACDT, UTC+10:30), as daylight saving begins on the first Sunday of October (October 4, 2026).
2. **Madrid Time Zone:** Madrid is observing Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2).
3. **Time Difference:** Adelaide is 8 hours and 30 minutes ahead of Madrid.
4. **Conversion:** Subtracting 8 hours and 30 minutes from 10:00 AM on October 6, 2026, gives 01:30 AM on October 6, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the local time in Madrid for the deadline:

1. **Sydney Time Zone (October 3, 2026):** Daylight Saving Time in New South Wales begins on the first Sunday of October (October 4, 2026). Therefore, on Saturday, October 3, 2026, Sydney is on Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST), which is **UTC+10**.
2. **Madrid Time Zone (October 3, 2026):** Madrid is observing Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is **UTC+2**.
3. **Time Difference:** Sydney is 8 hours ahead of Madrid (UTC+10 vs. UTC+2).
4. **Conversion:** Subtracting 8 hours from 18:00 (6:00 PM) gives 10:00 AM on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
